notes:
- Aegis builds ML-driven clinical triage and patient intake chatbot. Highly regulated; data residency and strict audit trails required.
- Current infra: hybrid cloud + private data centers; intent to start Dedicated with VPC and later move sensitive workloads on-prem.
- Main negotiation point: throughput guarantees. Customer: 'We need predictable throughput—if you promise 5k tokens/sec sustained, we need credits when below that, not just uptime.'
- SE findings: 8x A100-equivalent pool meets conversational latency targets on latest quantized model but margin for concurrency spikes is narrow.
- Proposed compromise from Redwood: guaranteed baseline (4.5k tokens/sec) with documented burst policy (2x for N minutes) + optional reserved buffer capacity for 6 months. Credits tiered: 10% monthly credit if baseline missed 2x/month, 30% if 5x/month. Legal pushing back on unlimited credits; suggested cap tied to monthly invoice.
- Concurrency: Aegis wants session-level fairness (per-customer concurrency caps) and ability to reserve concurrency for emergent triage flows. Redwood SE suggested soft caps with routing policy that prioritizes clinical flows and automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variant.
- Warmup & cache behavior: customer stressed cold-cache penalties — wants explicit SLA note that major restarts need 24h notice or grace period; otherwise credits apply.
- Cost sensitivity: they accept higher committed ARR for guaranteed throughput but expect predictable unit economics. Proposed 12-month reserved plan with scale triggers at 70% utilization.
- Open questions: exact credit math, definition of "sustained" (5-minute window vs. 15-minute), who pays for emergency burst capacity beyond contracted burst allowance.
- Next: legal to share redlined SLA by 2024-11-09; AE to coordinate exec demo focused on routing/fallback on 2024-11-15.
